title: SDK deferred-invocation hooks and language examples for streaming tool calls and structured outputs
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Existing SDKs expose both chunked streaming primitives and legacy sync-style tool call helpers. Customers upgrading to structured streaming tool outputs hit friction: SDK ergonomics differ across TS/Python/Go, testing is fragile, and small breaking changes in envelope formats caused observed regressions.

Goal: Provide a small, language-idiomatic 'deferred-invocation hook' surface that: 1) allows progressive (streaming) emission of structured tool events (metadata, partial results, final payload), 2) works with both existing non-streaming code paths (backwards compat) and new streaming pipelines, and 3) includes clear examples for TypeScript, Python, and Go to accelerate migrations.

Scope: API surface for SDKs (TS/Py/Go), adapter shim for legacy sync handlers, example reference implementations + tests, migration guide, and rollout plan for beta users. Not in scope: runtime-side kernel changes or server protocol format changes (those are tracked in infra tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Stable API in TypeScript, Python, and Go for deferred invocation hooks that supports progressive structured events
Backwards compatibility shim that maps legacy sync tool handlers to hook interface without changes to user code
Three language examples (TS/Py/Go) in the examples repo demonstrating streaming partials, metadata events, and final structured payload
Unit + integration tests demonstrating graceful fallback when streaming is unavailable
Migration guide in Confluence and short demo recorded for docs team
design_decisions: Choose a minimal hook signature: onEvent(eventType, payload, meta?) to avoid large surface area and make bindings lightweight
Represent structured events as typed 'envelope' objects with a stable discriminator string (e.g., 'meta' | 'partial' | 'result' | 'error') to simplify parsing in all languages
Provide an adapter function mapLegacyHandler(legacyHandler) that returns a deferred hook compatible wrapper — this avoids forcing immediate user changes
Stream framing remains JSON-lines over the existing protocol; SDKs parse incrementally and yield typed objects rather than raw strings
Keep error semantics explicit: 'error' envelopes must include code and userMessage for better UX in consoles and retriable logic
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and goals captured. Assigned to Ravi for implementation plan.

2026-02-23: Spike completed for TS and Py prototypes demonstrating onEvent hook; discovered minor perf overhead when parsing per-line JSON in Node streaming API. Decided to implement a small pooled decoder to reduce allocations.
2026-02-28: Proposed envelope contract posted to Confluence (link below). Added acceptance criteria and test matrix. Requested UX review from docs and console teams.
2026-03-05: PR opened for TypeScript shim and examples (GH PR #10234). Running CI; failing on a flaky test in Go adapter (race on map access).
2026-03-09: Go adapter race condition fixed by switching to channel-based emitter. Integration tests passing locally. Preparing demo for internal SDK alpha next week.
comments: Prashant (review): Can we make onEvent cancelable so callers can early-abort if downstream processing is slow? Concern: adds complexity to async adapters. — Suggested solution: return a boolean or a 'shouldContinue' Promise; prefer keep simple for v1.
Leah (docs): Examples are clear but please include a short migration snippet that shows how to replace 'syncCall' with 'invokeTool' + mapLegacyHandler to reassure customers.
Kait (security): Ensure envelope parsing does not allow prototype pollution in JS and map insertion attacks in Go. Add fuzz tests for untrusted payloads.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): Internal SDK team + docs team (1 week) - merge TS + Py examples behind feature flag
Phase 1 (beta): Invite 10 early customers via feature flag (3 weeks) - collect migration feedback and error reports
Phase 2 (general): Default enable in SDKs with migration doc and automated shim in CLI (4 weeks) - monitor error rates and adoption metrics
Rollback: feature flag at client runtime and server-side gating to disable streaming envelopes if regressions observed
notes: Trade-offs: A very small surface (single onEvent) avoids SDK churn but means some syntactic ceremony for language users. Larger helper objects would be nicer ergonomically but increase maintenance cost.
Testing: Plan includes cross-language golden fixtures containing a sequence of envelopes (meta, partial x N, result) plus malicious payload cases.
Observability: Add an SDK telemetry event 'hook_event_parsed' with minimal cardinality to help debug adoption without leaking payloads.
